sources.title: Development producer (Film and TV drama)
sources.source_location: The role profile anchors development as finding and shaping stories and scripts for commission or production; it documents a collaborative workflow, not a universal formula for creative quality.

sources.title: Applying for BFI NETWORK England short film funding
sources.source_location: The application record makes logline, story outline, creative vision, dates and production proposal inspectable development artefacts; it does not establish that one template guarantees commissioning.

sources.title: Production manager (Film and TV drama)
sources.source_location: The profile documents production management responsibilities for costs, future spending and coordination, separating managerial evidence from aesthetic authorship claims.

sources.title: Production coordinator (Film and TV drama)
sources.source_location: The profile identifies schedules, crew and cast lists, scripts and revisions as coordinated pre-production documents and supports analysis of versioned production information.

sources.title: Director (Film and TV drama)
sources.source_location: The role profile describes the director as a creative lead working with producers, casting and departments; it supports distributed decision analysis rather than sole-author mythology.

sources.title: Production designer (Film and TV drama)
sources.source_location: The profile documents production design as the organisation of the visible world of drama and anchors scenography, sets and interdepartmental work without reducing the result to decoration.

sources.title: Costume designer (Film and TV drama)
sources.source_location: The role profile anchors costume as researched, designed and produced screen work coordinated with other departments, supporting material rather than purely symbolic analysis.

sources.title: Casting director (Film and TV drama)
sources.source_location: The profile locates casting within production-company role matching and collaboration; it does not authorize identity inference or claims that an actor naturally is a role.

sources.title: Self-tape and Zoom auditions guidance
sources.source_location: Equity guidance prohibits nude or partially nude self-tapes and supports clear, bounded and professionally safe audition requests.

sources.title: Standards and Protocols for the Use of Intimacy Coordinators
sources.source_location: The protocol covers script breakdown, communication, choreography, nudity and simulated-sex safeguards and informed continuing consent; it does not transfer the performer's consent to a coordinator.

sources.title: Risikovurdering
sources.source_location: The guidance requires risk assessment to be adapted to purpose, activity and detail level, supporting production-specific assessment rather than a generic checklist claim.

sources.title: Forskrift om organisering, ledelse og medvirkning
sources.source_location: The authority explains planning, prevention, worker information and participation in risk assessment and work-system design.

sources.title: Standard arbeidsavtale for TV-underholdning
sources.source_location: The agreement links production plans and daily plans to expected working time and recording of actual work and overtime, providing a Norwegian labour-document case rather than a universal statutory summary.

sources.title: Screen Credits Manual
sources.source_location: The manual documents negotiated definitions and procedures for screenwriting credit, supporting the distinction between visible credit, performed work and contractual attribution.

sources.title: Nordisk bærekraftstandard – NES
sources.source_location: NFI's Nordic sustainability standard requires production awareness, responsibility and a sustainability coordinator; compliance claims remain distinct from measured emissions reduction.

sources.title: BAFTA albert launches revamped production carbon calculator and certification toolkit
sources.source_location: The record documents a screen-production carbon calculator and certification toolkit; calculation boundaries and reported actions must be named before reduction or neutrality is claimed.

sources.title: Making Audio and Video Media Accessible
sources.source_location: The guidance distinguishes captions, transcripts, described transcripts and description of visual information by user need; each is a designed production component, not an interchangeable label.

sources.title: Planning Audio and Video Media
sources.source_location: The planning guidance treats captions, descriptions and transcripts as project decisions to scope and resource early, supporting accessibility-by-design rather than end-stage remediation.

sources.title: Tilgjengelighet
sources.source_location: NRK documents current services including subtitling, sign-language interpretation and audio description and states its new-program subtitling practice; institutional practice is not proof that every user need is met.

sources.title: Introduction to USD
sources.source_location: The documentation explains USD as a system for collaboratively constructing and interchanging complex 3D scenes across authoring and rendering tools, supporting pipeline analysis rather than software-neutrality claims.

sources.publisher: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: Academy Color Encoding System: standardized production infrastructure for VFX
sources.source_location: The Academy record documents ACES as standardized production infrastructure connecting animation, VFX and colour-correction tools.

sources.title: In-Camera VFX Overview in Unreal Engine
sources.source_location: The documentation describes LED volume, camera tracking, real-time rendering and multi-user changes as a concrete ICVFX workflow; vendor capability is not independent proof of cost, labour or environmental benefit.

sources.title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
sources.source_location: The recommendation supplies human-rights, safety, transparency, cultural-diversity and governance principles; it is a normative framework, not evidence that a particular model or production is compliant.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence
sources.source_location: The WGA record documents negotiated AI protections for writers and frames employment, compensation and use of writers' work as labour-governance questions.

sources.title: Digital Replicas
sources.source_location: The guidance documents informed consent, reasonably specific use and compensation questions for performer digital replicas and distinguishes later-project use.

sources.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
sources.source_location: The report series separately addresses digital replicas, copyrightability of AI outputs and training issues, preventing one policy question from standing in for all AI governance.

sources.title: AI and Animation
sources.source_location: The union task force examines machine-learning use and potential automation effects on animation workers, supplying an affected-worker perspective rather than a neutral forecast.

sources.title: Actor: creative industries
sources.source_location: The role profile treats acting as skilled preparation, interpretation, rehearsal, performance and collaboration across screen and other creative media; it supports workflow description, not a universal acting technique.

sources.title: Groundbreaking LED Stage Production Technology Created for The Mandalorian
sources.source_location: ILM's dated production record names The Mandalorian Season One and documents its LED volume, camera tracking, real-time environments, practical set pieces, performers and department collaboration; first-party performance claims remain bounded as vendor evidence.
